toegepas.blok: Die sleutel sê wat die simbole beteken
toegepas.voor: sê nie altyd uit sy eie wat hy beteken nie
toegepas.na: sê nie altyd self wat hy beteken nie
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Uit sy eie' means 'of its own accord' and reads like a calque of 'on its own'; 'self' is the natural Afrikaans here (net -2 words).
toegepas.fout: 'uit sy eie' is a loose, English-shaped phrase here ('on its own'); natural Afrikaans says 'self'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Sê nie altyd self wat hy beteken nie' is the natural wording, shorter, and keeps the meaning and the qualifier 'altyd'.

toegepas.voor: Iemand anders kan jou kaart makliker lees as jou simbole in 'n sleutel staan.
toegepas.na: As jou simbole in 'n sleutel staan, kan iemand anders jou kaart makliker lees.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Makliker lees as' first reads as a comparison ('easier than your symbols'); putting the conditional clause first removes the ambiguity without changing the meaning (net 0 words).
toegepas.fout: 'makliker lees as jou simbole' first reads as a comparison, so a reader stumbles on the conditional 'as'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Putting the condition first removes the garden-path reading without changing who does what, and the comma after a leading subordinate clause is correct.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: After an instruction ('Lees eers die sleutel'), 'dan' expresses the result that follows; 'nou' wrongly suggests the reader already did it (net 0 words).
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Nou weet jy' after an instruction is ordinary, natural instructional Afrikaans; 'Dan' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The next sentence says 'of jy reg geraai het', so switching from 'n mens to jy within two sentences is inconsistent; using jy throughout keeps the reference steady (net -1 word).
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Moving from the general ''n mens' to 'jy' within a paragraph is normal Afrikaans, and the generic sense (any reader) is what the sentence means; the proposal is only different.
